# Supermatter Delamination
Supermatter delamination occurs when the crystal exceeds its ability to maintain structural recovery.
During this event, the crystal enters an uncontrolled instability state and begins producing additional reaction byproducts, accelerating the failure process.
## Emergency Response
If engineering personnel fail to maintain minimum operational standards, immediate corrective action is required.
Follow Nanotrasen Engineering emergency procedures.
## Delamination Prevention
Priority actions:
1. Remove destabilizing components.
2. Remove unsuitable chamber conditions and correct their source.
3. Deploy Nanotrasen standard-issued metal foam containment equipment.
Failure to stabilize the Supermatter will result in a complete cascade event.
## Final Emergency Procedures
If delamination cannot be stopped:
1. Inform the crew of possible Supermatter failure. 2. Advise evacuation to emergency shelters or shuttle evacuation. 3. Distribute approved protective equipment. 4. Prepare engineering equipment for post-event recovery operations.
## Delamination Cleanup
Once the Supermatter reaches critical instability, the original crystal structure will collapse and transform into cascade crystals.
Cascade crystals rapidly expand and replace surrounding structures with their altered crystalline structure.
These structures cannot be removed with standard tools.
Specialized Nanotrasen engineering equipment is required for safe removal.
Personnel should avoid unnecessary interaction with cascade structures until the area has been declared safe.
